process_description: The H2/N2 gas mixing and receiver tank system receives customer-side N2 100% and H2 100% gas supplies through intake filters and pressure regulators. The regulated gas streams enter the A-IET scope, where H2 is routed to Gas Mixer MG 100-2ME(Ex) and the mixed hydrogen-containing gas is transferred to a 500 L stainless-steel receiver tank. The receiver tank buffers the mixed gas before normal delivery to the downstream Process at approximately 4.5-5 bar through SV (21.1) and CV (12.1). An H2 Analyzer with Auto Calibration monitors hydrogen concentration and communicates with Control & Display, HMI Programming, and Emergency Control. During abnormal hydrogen concentration or pressure conditions, the emergency control logic can isolate the normal outlet, introduce N2 through the emergency purge line, and discharge or flush gas to roof through the vent path.
intention: The system is designed to provide filtered, pressure-regulated, and monitored H2/N2 mixed gas to the downstream process while maintaining receiver tank buffering and safe operating pressure. The intended operation is to regulate the incoming gases to approximately 8 bar before the gas mixing section, store the mixed gas in a 500 L stainless-steel receiver tank with a maximum pressure rating of 10 bar, and supply the downstream process at approximately 4.5-5 bar. The safety objective is to prevent unsafe hydrogen concentration or pressure conditions from reaching the downstream process by using H2 concentration monitoring, emergency isolation of SV-21.1, N2 purge/flush through SV-21.3 and CV-12.3, and vent/flush discharge to roof through SV-21.2 and CV-12.2.
system_outputs: Mixed H2/N2 gas to downstream Process
Control/alarm indication to Control & Display, HMI Programming, and Emergency Control

connections.node: H2/N2 Gas Mixing and Receiver Tank System including customer-side N2 100% and H2 100% supply lines through intake filters and pressure regulators, H2 feed to Gas Mixer MG 100-2ME(Ex), mixed gas transfer to the 500 L stainless-steel receiver tank, receiver tank monitoring by H2 Analyzer with Auto Calibration, normal outlet line from the receiver tank to the downstream Process through SV (21.1) and CV (12.1), and emergency N2 purge/flush line with emergency control and vent discharge to roof.
connections.node_boundary: The grouped HAZOP node starts at the customer-side N2 100% and H2 100% supply lines upstream of the intake filters and pressure regulators. It includes the N2 and H2 intake filters, pressure regulation assemblies, feed isolation/check valves, Gas Mixer MG 100-2ME(Ex), mixed gas transfer line through SV (27), 500 L stainless-steel Receiver Tank TK-500L, H2 Analyzer with Auto Calibration, Control & Display, HMI Programming, Emergency Control logic, normal receiver outlet line through SV (21.1) and CV (12.1), emergency N2 purge/flush line through SV (21.3) and CV (12.3), receiver vent/flush line through MV, SV (21.2), CV (12.2), FA device, and final discharge to roof. The node ends at the downstream Process connection after SV (21.1)/CV (12.1) and at the roof vent discharge endpoint for emergency flushing.
connections.from_id: Nitrogen 100% customer-side supply and Hydrogen 100% customer-side supply
connections.to_id: Mixed H2/N2 gas to downstream Process and Emergency vent/flush gas to roof
connections.flow_direction: Mainstream operation: N2 100% and H2 100% enter from customer-side supplies, pass through intake filters and pressure regulators, and are regulated to approximately 8 bar before entering the A-IET gas mixing scope. H2 is routed to Gas Mixer MG 100-2ME(Ex), then mixed hydrogen-containing gas flows through SV (27) to the 500 L stainless-steel Receiver Tank TK-500L. The receiver tank buffers the mixed gas and normally discharges at approximately 4.5-5 bar through SV (21.1) and CV (12.1) to the downstream Process. Emergency operation: when abnormal hydrogen concentration or pressure is detected, the H2 Analyzer, Control & Display, HMI Programming, and Emergency Control logic can close SV (21.1), open SV (21.3) to admit N2 purge/flush gas through CV (12.3), and open SV (21.2) so gas from TK-500L is flushed through CV (12.2), FA-1, and the vent line to roof. Control and signal flow travels between H2 Analyzer, Control & Display, HMI Programming, and Emergency Control, supported by the electrical power supply.
connections.context: This grouped node is intentionally defined as one mainstream HAZOP reasoning package rather than narrow equipment-to-equipment pipe segments. It allows the LLM to reason across cross-boundary effects where a cause located in one part of the P&ID can produce consequences in another part of the same operating system. For example, low N2 pressure or blocked N2 filter can affect purge effectiveness, receiver inerting/flush capability, emergency recovery, and downstream gas composition. H2 feed regulator failure, H2 isolation valve malfunction, or H2 check valve leakage can affect mixer composition, receiver hydrogen concentration, and downstream flammability risk. SV (27) failure can affect receiver filling, mixer backpressure, and emergency isolation. SV (21.1) or CV (12.1) failure can affect downstream Process supply, reverse flow prevention, and emergency isolation. SV (21.2), CV (12.2), FA-1, or roof vent impairment can prevent safe vent/flush discharge. SV (21.3) or CV (12.3) failure can prevent N2 emergency purge. H2 Analyzer, Control & Display, HMI Programming, Emergency Control, pressure indicators, and signal wiring are included because they provide monitoring, alarm, logic, and protective action for concentration and pressure deviations. This node should therefore be used for cause-consequence-safeguard-recommendation generation, while line_level_connections should be used only for traceability back to physical P&ID segments. Typical deviation reasoning should consider No/Less Flow, More Flow, Reverse Flow, High Pressure, Low Pressure, High H2 concentration, Low H2 concentration, analyzer/control failure, isolation failure, purge failure, vent blockage, and loss of power/control signal. Safeguards include H2 Analyzer with Auto Calibration, Emergency Control logic, SV (21.1) outlet isolation, SV (21.3) N2 emergency purge, CV (12.3) purge backflow prevention, SV (21.2) vent opening, CV (12.2) vent backflow prevention, CV (12.1) process-line backflow prevention, local pressure indicators, Control & Display, HMI Programming, alarms, and procedural investigation after failed recovery.
